firefighter.label: Working Firefighter
firefighter.summary: Refresh high-consequence fundamentals while broadening judgment, health practices and mentoring.
guide: Decision quality
Read smoke/fire/building/occupancy and communicate meaningful changes early.
Coordination
Understand how attack, search, ventilation, water, ladders, RIT and command interact.
Mayday
Practice emergency traffic, self-rescue and firefighter rescue before you need it.
Health
Exposure reduction, sleep, cardiovascular fitness, heat/noise and behavioral health.
Mentoring
Demonstrate, explain the standard, observe, give specific feedback and repeat.
cards: Good fireground observation?
Specific, relevant and timely information tied to location/change.
Why rehearse Mayday skills?
Rare high-consequence tasks degrade without practice.
Coordinated search?
Search priorities synchronized with fire conditions, suppression, ventilation, staffing and command.
Experience in career development?
Relevant responsibility and demonstrated work, not simply years elapsed.
What to study before promotion?
The next role's decisions, people responsibility, policies and communication—not only a test bank.
quiz: Newer member is correct but slow.
Coach one or two efficiency points and repeat safely
USFA treats relevant experience as its own development pillar.
next: Take on a project or mentoring responsibility.

driver.label: Driver / Operator
driver.summary: Safe driving, strategic placement, pump systems, hydraulics, water supply, troubleshooting and communication.
guide: Driving/placement
Arrive safely and position for access, hose, water, aerials, hazards and later units.
Pump systems
Know intake/discharge paths, gauges, governors/relief, primer and abnormal indications.
Hydraulics
Nozzle pressure, friction loss, elevation, appliances, standpipes and master streams.
Water supply
Hydrants, static/residual, LDH, drafting, tenders and relay concepts.
Troubleshooting
Recognize weak supply, pressure changes, overheating and line/device changes.
cards: Operator's first job before math?
Get the apparatus and crew there safely and position for operations.
Why watch residual pressure?
Its change while flowing helps judge how supply responds to demand.
Practical cavitation meaning?
The pump is not receiving enough water for the demand.
Why know actual hose/nozzle packages?
Real targets depend on department equipment and SOPs, not generic coefficients alone.
Why mental math if calculators exist?
It provides a reasonableness check and backup.
quiz: Residual drops sharply as more lines open.
A large residual change is a water-supply clue.
Correct pump math but poor placement equals:
Only one part of operator performance
Operator competence includes driving, placement, systems and communication.
